title: Battle of Stalingrad
summary: German air attacks on Stalingrad on the Volga began on the evening of 23 August 1942, opening a battle that ran until early February 1943. A Soviet counteroffensive from mid-November 1942 encircled more than 220,000 German soldiers, and about 91,000 survivors surrendered. The National WWII Museum cites up to 70,000 lives lost in the bombing and a death toll above 1,000,000 per historian Jochen Hellbeck, with numbers contested.

uncertainty.note: museum-digital dates the battle 23 August 1942 to 2 February 1943; the National WWII Museum describes the evening air raid of 23 August; the USHMM entry is dated 2 February 1943. Other sources may date the ground battle later.

audience_note: Describes aerial bombing of a city, civilian deaths and very high military casualties.

related.because: The National WWII Museum says Stalingrad shattered the image of Nazi invincibility and inspired resistance movements across occupied Europe, including the Warsaw Ghetto.
